long_biography.plain_text:
After a short spell at Morgan Stanley in New York, Mohammed Abdul Aziz Alshaya returned to Kuwait and rejoined a trading business his family had run since 1890. The company already held several Mothercare franchises, but Alshaya was asked to accelerate retail expansion. Appointed chief executive in 1990 and later executive chairman, he used franchise partnerships to take the business across the Middle East, North Africa, Türkiye and Europe.

Under his leadership, Alshaya Group built a broad consumer portfolio embracing fashion, coffee shops, restaurants, beauty, pharmacy and home furnishings, operating brands such as Starbucks and H&M. He also chairs Mabanee, the listed developer behind The Avenues shopping centres, and is identified as a major shareholder. His record therefore combines succession within an established family enterprise with substantial personal expansion of its retail platform and continuing oversight of retail property.
